h1: The 5 Best Leaf Blower Vacuum Combos of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Leaf Blower Vacuum Combos: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five leaf blower, vacuum and mulcher combos, from cord-free kits to budget electrics, with the tradeoffs of each.
summary: The WORX Trivac 3-in-1 is our top pick for a yard that needs one tool to blow, vacuum and mulch. The EGO Power+ LV5000 is the cord-free pick with the highest listed airflow at 500 CFM. The BLACK+DECKER combo kit suits buyers who want a battery tool at a middle price, while the MZK and Heywork are the lowest-cost ways in.
intro: A combo that blows, vacuums and mulches can replace two tools, but only if the conversion between modes is something you will actually do. Plenty of buyers pick the most powerful number on the page and then dread switching the tube, so the spec that matters first is how you plan to use it.

We reviewed five combos using their spec sheets and listing details and ranked them on power source, airflow, versatility and price bucket. Where the listing gave no airflow or speed figure, we say so rather than guess.

products.name: WORX Trivac 3-in-1 Electric Leaf Blower/Leaf Vacuum/Leaf Mulcher
products.verdict: The most complete blower, vacuum and mulcher in one electric unit.
products.description:
The WORX Trivac is an electric 3-in-1 that works as a leaf blower, a leaf vacuum and a leaf mulcher. It sits in the $50-100 price bucket. The listing gives no airflow figure, so the ranking leans on its three-mode design.

It takes first place because it is the only pick here that combines all three jobs with a proven electric design at a mid-range bucket. It costs more than the MZK and Heywork below, which also advertise three jobs.

It suits homeowners with a small to medium yard who want one tool. The caveat is that, being electric, it needs a cord and outlet reach.
products.idealFor: Homeowners wanting one electric tool for leaf cleanup.
products.skipIf: You need cordless freedom across a large yard.

products.name: EGO Power+ LV5000 Leaf Vacuum and Mulcher with 500 CFM Blower
products.verdict: Battery-powered with a stated 500 CFM blower.
products.description:
The EGO Power+ LV5000 is a battery-powered leaf vacuum and mulcher with a 500 CFM blower. It sits in the $200-500 bucket, the highest here.

It ranks second only because of price. It has a stated airflow and cord-free design that the WORX does not list, but it costs several buckets more.

It suits owners of bigger yards who value freedom from a cord. The caveat is the price bucket, and you should check whether the battery is included before buying.
products.idealFor: Larger yards where a cord is a nuisance.
products.skipIf: You want to spend as little as possible.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Leaf Blower Cordless Leaf Vacuum and Mulcher Combo Kit
products.verdict: A battery-powered kit with a 120 MPH blower at a middle price.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER combo kit pairs a cordless leaf blower with a leaf vacuum and mulcher. The listing states 120 MPH and battery power. It is in the $100-200 price bucket.

It sits below the EGO because 120 MPH is a speed figure, not airflow, so it is harder to compare with the EGO's 500 CFM. It costs less than the EGO yet more than the WORX.

It works for buyers who want cordless operation without the top price bucket. The caveat is the missing CFM figure.
products.idealFor: Cordless buyers who stop short of the top price bucket.
products.skipIf: You want a stated CFM rating.

products.name: Heywork 3-in-1 Leaf Vacuum Mulcher
products.description:
The Heywork 3-in-1 leaf vacuum mulcher lists 450 CFM of airflow. It sits in the $25-50 bucket, the lowest in this group.

It beats the MZK below because it states an airflow number, though it trails the WORX on how much we can verify about it.

It suits shoppers who want 3-in-1 behavior at the lowest cost. The caveat is that the listing is thin on other specs.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting a stated airflow figure.
products.skipIf: You want a well-documented spec sheet.

products.name: MZK 3-in-1 Electric Leaf Blower Vacuum Mulcher
products.verdict: An electric 3-in-1 in the lowest price bucket.
products.description:
The MZK is an electric blower, vacuum and mulcher in one, in the $25-50 bucket. The listing gives no airflow or speed figure.

It ranks last because the Heywork at least states a CFM number, and the WORX offers a better-known design a bucket up.

It works for occasional users with a small yard. The caveat is that its performance is not documented in the listing.
products.idealFor: Occasional users with a small yard.

whatMatters.detail: CFM measures air volume moved, while MPH measures air speed at the nozzle. Volume matters for pushing wet or heavy piles, and speed matters for lifting stuck debris. Look for both numbers in the bullets, and distrust a listing that gives neither.

A corded electric combo runs as long as you have an outlet, while a battery tool gives freedom but limited runtime. The choice matters on larger yards where an extension cord gets in the way. Check whether the battery and charger are included in the box.
A mulcher shreds leaves so they take up less space in a bag. This matters if you collect and bag leaves instead of blowing them away. Confirm the listing says mulcher, not just vacuum.
Combos need you to swap tubes or attachments between jobs. If that is awkward you will skip using the vacuum. Read the listing for how the conversion works.
A lower bucket often means fewer documented specs. That matters because you cannot compare what is not stated. Treat missing numbers as a reason to ask questions, not as a good sign.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: No runtime limit but tied to an outlet. The WORX Trivac and MZK are electric.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: Freedom to move, limited by battery. The EGO LV5000 and BLACK+DECKER kit are battery powered.

howToChoose.note: Small yards can stay corded, larger yards should go cordless.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: An electric tool that does all three jobs without a big price.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The WORX Trivac 3-in-1 covers blow, vacuum and mulch in the $50-100 bucket.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your yard is large and a cord is a problem, so the EGO Power+ LV5000 earns its bucket.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only clear leaves a few times a season, where the Heywork or MZK is enough.

faq.q: Can one tool really blow, vacuum and mulch?
faq.a: Yes, the combos here advertise all three. You usually swap an attachment between jobs.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with these?
faq.a: Buying on the biggest number without checking the power source. A cord can limit a large yard.

faq.q: Is the EGO worth it over the WORX?
faq.a: Only if you want cordless and a stated 500 CFM. Otherwise the WORX is a lower bucket for the same three jobs.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Attach the tube for your chosen mode and follow the listing's conversion steps. Read the manual before first use.

faq.q: How do I maintain a mulcher?
faq.a: Clear the intake and the bag after use. Keep the inlet free of wet clumps.

faq.q: Does a listing that lacks CFM mean it is weak?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but you cannot verify it. Treat the missing number as a gap.

finalTake: The WORX Trivac 3-in-1 is the safest buy for most yards. Step up to the EGO Power+ LV5000 only if you want cordless power and a stated 500 CFM. If you just want the cheapest way in, the Heywork lists airflow, while the MZK gives you less to go on.
